government.note: Government type as on 1 January 2000: a directly elected President (five-year term) with a Prime Minister appointed by the President and dependent on the National Assembly. The constitutional amendments approved in the December 2015 referendum created a parliamentary system: since April 2018 the President is elected by the National Assembly for a single seven-year term and the Prime Minister heads the executive (per the Wikipedia articles on the President and Prime Minister of Armenia). The type and power weights are kept as in 2000.

system.note: In 1999: 56 seats by national party-list PR and 75 in single-member constituencies (131 seats). Since 2017 the Assembly is elected by party-list PR with at least 101 seats plus additional seats (105 in 2017, 132 in 2018, 107 in 2021, 105 in 2026) and a five-year term. Threshold not checked. seats_2000 is the result of the May 1999 election, not adjusted for the deputies killed in the parliament shooting of 27 October 1999. The four-year term is inferred from the 1999-2003-2007 cycle.

chambers.review_note: Seats held on 1 January 2000 may differ from the May 1999 result because of the deaths in the October 1999 shooting; the pre-2017 term length (four years) is inferred from the election cycle.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the May 1999 party-list vote (shares of all valid list votes): Unity Bloc 41.45% (RPA and People's Party; big tent), Law and Unity 7.93% and other lists without a seat about 16.8% (big tent); Armenian Communist Party 12.04% plus the Union of Communist and Socialist Parties 2.48% (Marxist-Leninist); ARF 7.79% (democratic socialist); Orinats Yerkir 5.25% (liberal conservative); National Democratic Union 5.14% and Pan-Armenian National Movement 1.16% (centrist liberal).
